narrative: Britta Mäkinen's tickets show a recurring API rate-limit fault that resurfaced in September ("the API rate limit problem we reported in June has returned... This is the second time we have had to raise this") and again per the February 2025 ticket ("the API rate limit issue from last year came back in December and took weeks to stabilise"), despite each ticket being closed as resolved. The account has adopted a workaround ("we have adjusted our retry logic as a workaround but it should not be necessary") and is now also blocked by a missing feature (running totals) during a time-sensitive annual reporting cycle. Tone has shifted from neutral to openly frustrated ("this is getting frustrating") with no confirmation the underlying issues are actually fixed.

A sparse but telling pattern: an API totals-inconsistency ticket was left explicitly unresolved in October 2024, and a year later the customer is still only checking in passively ("wanted to check whether the inconsistent totals issue from last October was ever tracked down, or if it's since resolved itself"). The large-report export timeout also recurred in April 2025 ("the large-report export timeout from last year is back... wondering if there's a size limit we should just plan around instead"), with the customer now proposing to design around the bug rather than expect a fix. Low volume and calm tone mask two faults that were never genuinely closed out.

A rough stretch — a dashboard access fault sat open for nine months while API, connector, and report-builder problems piled on top, prompting a formal escalation ("I need someone to take ownership of the whole account, not individual tickets") — was followed by a real fix: dashboard access was confirmed restored and holding ("has been restored properly... and has held for several days. Genuinely relieved"), alerts came back, and the account has since placed calm, expansionary tickets (new seats, a second connector, routine alert tweaks). This is a recovered relationship, not a failing one.

Anna Leinonen's account ends mid-crisis: a scheduled SFTP export has failed twice in a month under a false "Completed" status ("the SFTP export failed again last night. Same issue as September... I have been patient but this is a pattern now"), and a dashboard drill-down fault reported the day before is still broken. The history stops immediately after this angry, unresolved ticket, with no further contact to confirm either issue was ever fixed — a silent-churn signature rather than a healthy quiet patch.

A low-volume, largely positive account ("working well overall – one question...") whose recent tickets are unanswered feature requests rather than faults: an SSO setup question and a role-based dashboard tile-visibility request both sit unresolved, with a follow-up two weeks later showing the first hint of impatience ("or should we look at a workaround in report builder instead?"). Nothing here indicates a broken fault or eroded trust, just requests waiting on a response.

Five routine, well-spaced tickets over three months — SSL certificate questions, a timezone check, a template-locking question — all handled quickly and without complaint. One minor item (alerts firing outside business hours) was left unresolved but never followed up on. This reads as a healthy, low-touch account.

A genuinely rough year (six incidents in nine months across API, connectors, alerts, and exports) escalated to demands for root-cause answers and a senior call ("we need a root-cause explanation, not another quick patch"; "we need a call with someone senior at Kataja, not another ticket"), but the call happened and it worked: subsequent tickets confirm stability ("API calls have been clean since we adjusted the rate limits", "the new alert thresholds have caught two real issues before they became problems") and the account is now expanding, asking about a second ERP connector. A textbook recovered-after-escalation account.

A modest, largely uneventful account with occasional bugs (a stale distribution list, an export column that went missing then returned blank for EMEA entities) each fixed within days with no pattern of recurrence beyond a same-week follow-up. Tone stays calm and matter-of-fact throughout ("quick one", "everything else looks fine"). No sign of accumulating frustration or genuinely open threads.

An entirely routine account — API token renewal, seat administration, SSO group mapping, a conditional-formatting question — with every ticket resolved without complaint or recurrence. No evidence of friction at all.

A cluster of sharp, high-pressure tickets (a blank dashboard before a Monday meeting, a locked-out new hire, a connector failing twice in a week) recurs in January 2025 when a dashboard fix "held for about three hours and then the same timeout came back", immediately followed by a permissions regression from that same patch. Tone throughout questions the platform's reliability ("the kind of outage that makes people ask why we're paying for this") and demands fixes actually hold ("confirm this is actually fixed this time, not just restarted"), and the account then goes quiet with no further tickets — fixes not holding plus abrupt silence is a concerning signal, not a reassuring one.

The account raised a custom-SQL execution timeout in June 2024 and chased it politely through October ("a poor use of a data engineer's time given what this platform is meant to replace") before quietly building a permanent manual workaround: "we've rebuilt that particular report entirely around smaller queries plus a manual Excel merge step, which our team now owns end to end... nobody has to think about it each quarter anymore." A second export-timeout fault got identical treatment, with the closing ticket explicitly deprioritising both ("not expecting this to jump the queue... if either gets picked up at all"). This is the quiet-resignation pattern — polite, low-volume, and the customer has stopped expecting the product to work.

A quiet account with one slow export delivery (11 days) and one self-flagged low-priority display bug ("low priority but flagging it so it's on record") left open without complaint. The most recent ticket is a routine, forward-looking feature question about merging data sources. Nothing suggests declining trust.

A dashboard external-sharing request from June 2024 "never really got a clear answer", forcing the customer into a manual Excel-export workaround they explicitly say became normal ("nobody flags it as a problem day to day"); a freight-connector sync delay got identical treatment ("we've adjusted our morning review to simply build in that lag as expected rather than chase it further"). The closing ticket ties both to a looming commercial decision — "we're not expecting a change here before our contract review next year, so no need to prioritise it" — the quiet, resigned pattern that precedes non-renewal.
A small number of calm, professional inquiries (API access, a formula question, a dashboard slowdown) all resolved without complaint or recurrence. No signs of friction anywhere in the history.

One alert-configuration request from December wasn't actually working ("the alert we asked you to configure back in December hasn't triggered even though we've had two sync failures since") — a real gap between what was asked for and what was delivered — but it was fixed. The account's most recent ticket is a forward-looking pilot of a new API integration, suggesting continued and even expanding engagement.

Ingrid Dahl's account shows the clearest deterioration in the batch: dashboard filter persistence and API 429 errors both sit unresolved with no follow-up, a margin alert fault was "supposedly resolved" but recurred twice more with dates meticulously documented ("14 April, threshold crossed at 11.2%, no alert. 28 April, same alert, no trigger"), and an export-truncation ticket states outright "this is the same issue, not resolved" despite being logged as resolved. Tone has escalated to an explicit demand for senior attention ("I need someone senior to look at our account"), and the breadth of genuinely open faults across alerts, dashboards, API, and exports is unusually wide.

A chronically noisy account with frequent incidents across every module (connectors failing three times in one day, dashboard outages, API 500s and an unannounced key rotation, alert false-positive fatigue), but every incident gets fixed within a day or two and the customer keeps coming back and using the product hard rather than pulling away. Frustration is real and recurring ("I've lost count of how many times this year", "I'd like to know what the actual fix is, not just another rerun") but incident frequency has thinned from dense weekly clusters in 2024 to isolated single tickets in 2025, with no workaround-building or disengagement in the text — an engaged, if impatient, heavy user rather than an account heading for the door.

A light-touch account with one non-urgent open item (a greyed-out export button the customer themselves called "not urgent") and a couple of quickly-fixed webhook bugs, otherwise routine admin and report-builder questions. No frustration or recurrence anywhere in the history.

A wide, chronic spread of unresolved faults across nine months — a dashboard iframe-embed problem, a dashboard/report total discrepancy still "not matching" after a fix, a missing API field blocking the customer's own monitoring build, and a report scheduler sending to wrong recipients that had already recurred once — culminates in a December ticket citing three simultaneous open tickets and asking outright "at what point does someone senior review our account?" No response to that question appears before the history ends. A broad, unaddressed reliability problem rather than an isolated complaint.

Just two tickets, both positive — thanks for a feature rollout with a minor refinement request, and a request to add seats for team expansion. A short history, but every signal (gratitude, growth, no complaints) points toward a healthy, engaged account.
